# FDGD059

> PERMITTED: Changing Runtime Error Exceptions to Usage Error Exceptions

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section D.12.1 Changing Runtime Error Exceptions to Usage Error Exceptions. Applies to: runtime break.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Example: throwing `ArgumentNullException` instead of `NullReferenceException`, or `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` instead of `IndexOutOfRangeException`. PublicApiAnalyzers (optional in /fdg-setup) can flag changes to the public API.

## From the book

If your method throws a `NullReferenceException` when a parameter is passed as `null`, or an `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a parameter is passed as an out-of-bounds index, you can change it to throw the usage error equivalent exception (e.g., `ArgumentNullException` or `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`) instead. While some callers could, conceivably, depend on the `NullReferenceException` or `IndexOutOfRangeException`, the .NET BCL team believes that the information provided via the usage error exception about which argument value caused the method to fail is worth the risk.

The .NET BCL team generally considers changing “failed inputs” to “a detailed usage error exception” to be an acceptable breaking change.
